Furthermore, the presence of this default key in a shared environment (like AUR) increases the risk that it will be exploited at scale, especially if users deploy the service without reviewing configuration defaults. Although the file itself is a configuration file and not executable code, distributing it with a hardcoded, widely-known secret constitutes a supply chain risk.
